item.title: UAE asks U.S. for dollar swap line as Iran war strains economy
item.description:
The United Arab Emirates has quietly initiated discussions with the United States about a potential financial safety net as the war with Iran continues to strain its economy, according to a report by The Wall Street Journal on Saturday.

UAE Central Bank Governor Khaled Mohamed Balama raised the idea of a dollar currency-swap line with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Federal Reserve officials during meetings in Washington last week, where the Central Bank of the UAE was participating in the IMF and World Bank spring meetings. U.S. officials described the overture as precautionary rather than a formal request, with Emirati representatives stressing that they have so far managed to avoid the worst economic consequences of the conflict but may still need a backstop.

item.title: US-Iran talks set for Monday as ceasefire nears expiration
item.description: The fate of Iran's enriched uranium stockpile has emerged as the central obstacle in ongoing negotiations between Washington and Tehran, with President Donald Trump claiming Iran "has agreed to everything" even as Iranian officials flatly reject any transfer of nuclear material abroad. A new round of talks is expected in Islamabad on Tuesday, April 21, with a fragile ceasefire set to expire by midweek.

item.title: China tests microwave beam to recharge drones midair
item.description:
Chinese scientists have demonstrated a system that wirelessly transmits power from a ground vehicle to a drone in flight using microwave energy, a development that could one day allow unmanned aircraft to stay airborne indefinitely.

The research, published on March 25 in the peer-reviewed Chinese journal Aeronautical Science & Technology, was carried out by a team from Xidian University, an institution known for its military technology work, according to the South China Morning Post. The system uses a car-mounted microwave emitter to beam energy to an antenna array fitted to the drone's underside — and critically, it works while both the vehicle and the aircraft are moving.

item.title: Iran adviser warns of wider sea conflict as Hormuz tightens again
item.description: Ali Akbar Velayati, a senior advisor to Iran's Supreme Leader Seyyed Mojtaba Khamenei, declared on Sunday that the era of Western powers imposing security "from across the oceans" has ended, warning that "any mischief will trigger a chain reaction." The remarks, posted on X, came as Iran doubled down on restricting maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and signaled that the conflict could extend to other global shipping chokepoints, including the Bab al-Mandeb strait off Yemen's coast.

item.title: Israel building permanent military bases in Gaza, satellite images show
item.description: An investigation by Al Jazeera's Digital Investigations Unit, drawing on satellite imagery from Planet Labs and Sentinel Hub, has revealed that Israel is systematically building permanent military infrastructure across Gaza, even as civilian reconstruction efforts have stalled and aid organizations describe the Trump administration's ceasefire plan as a failure.

item.title: Oil prices surge as US Navy seizes Iranian ship near Hormuz
item.description: Oil prices jumped sharply on Sunday after the US Navy fired upon and seized an Iranian-flagged cargo ship attempting to bypass the American blockade of Iranian ports, capping a chaotic weekend that saw Tehran reimpose controls over the Strait of Hormuz and dash hopes of a swift reopening of the critical waterway.

item.title: UniCredit unveils plan to transform Commerzbank
item.description: UniCredit is set to present its strategy for transforming Commerzbank on Monday, April 20, escalating its long-running pursuit of the German lender by publicly laying out a vision it says will make the bank "future-ready."

item.title: Samsung SDI signs first EV battery deal with Mercedes-Benz
item.description:
Samsung SDI announced Monday that it has signed a multi-year agreement with Mercedes-Benz to supply batteries for the automaker's electric vehicles, marking the first time the South Korean battery maker's cells will power a Mercedes model.

The batteries will use high-nickel NCM (nickel, cobalt, and manganese) chemistry and are destined for Mercedes-Benz's next-generation compact and mid-size electric SUVs and coupe models, Samsung SDI said in a statement. The company did not disclose the financial terms of the deal.

item.title: 7.5-magnitude earthquake off Japan triggers tsunami warnings
item.description:
A powerful earthquake struck off the northeastern coast of Japan on Monday afternoon, prompting tsunami warnings across several prefectures and shaking buildings as far south as Tokyo. The Japan Meteorological Agency reported the quake hit at 4:53 p.m. local time in the Pacific waters off Iwate prefecture, registering a preliminary magnitude of 7.5 at a shallow depth of about 10 kilometers below the sea surface.

The JMA warned that tsunami waves of up to 3 meters could reach the northern shoreline, urging residents to evacuate immediately from coastal and riverside areas to higher ground. Tsunami warnings — the second-highest level of alert — were issued for the Pacific coasts of Iwate, Aomori, and southeastern Hokkaido, while milder advisories were posted for the coasts of Miyagi and Fukushima to the south.

item.title: Second round of US-Iran talks set to begin amid uranium standoff
item.description: The fate of Iran's enriched uranium stockpile has emerged as the central obstacle in US-Iran negotiations, with Washington demanding Tehran relinquish the material and Iran insisting it will not be "transferred anywhere" — even as a fragile ceasefire nears expiration on April 22.

item.title: Eni announces giant gas discovery offshore Indonesia
item.description:
Eni announced on Monday a giant gas discovery at the Geliga-1 exploration well in the Ganal block of the Kutei Basin, offshore Indonesia, with preliminary estimates pointing to in-place resources of approximately 5 trillion cubic feet of gas and 300 million barrels of condensate.

The find adds to a string of deepwater successes for the Italian energy company in Southeast Asia and could pave the way for a third production hub in one of Indonesia's most prolific offshore basins.

item.title: UAE warns it may settle oil trades in yuan without US dollar backstop
item.description: The United Arab Emirates has warned the United States that it may begin settling oil and gas transactions in Chinese yuan if Washington fails to provide a dollar liquidity backstop, according to the Wall Street Journal. The threat marks a striking fracture in the petrodollar system at a moment when the ongoing war between the US and Iran has strained Gulf economies and called into question American security commitments in the region.

item.title: Iran refuses fresh peace talks as ceasefire nears expiry
item.description: The war between the United States, Israel, and Iran — now in its 51st day — is sending shockwaves through the world economy, disrupting energy supplies on an unprecedented scale and prompting the International Monetary Fund to cut its global growth forecast as hopes for a lasting ceasefire dim.

item.title: Iran pulls out of US talks after ship seizure
item.description:
The United States military fired on and seized an Iranian-flagged cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman on Sunday, the first known use of force in Washington's naval blockade of Iranian ports, throwing a fragile ceasefire into crisis less than 48 hours before it is set to expire.

U.S. Central Command said the guided-missile destroyer USS Spruance intercepted the Touska, a 294-meter cargo vessel, as it sailed through the Arabian Sea toward the Iranian port of Bandar Abbas. After the crew ignored repeated warnings, the warship used its deck gun to disable the vessel's engine room, and Marines from the 31st Marine Expeditionary Unit boarded from helicopters launched off the amphibious assault ship USS Tripoli.

President Donald Trump announced the seizure on Truth Social, writing that the ship had been "stopped right in its tracks by a hole in the engine room" and that Marines had taken control. The Touska and its owners were already under U.S. Treasury sanctions for allegedly helping Iran evade trade restrictions.

item.title: UK pushes for toll-free Hormuz as ceasefire nears expiry
item.description: Britain's Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper has intensified diplomatic efforts to secure unrestricted navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, warning that the waterway must reopen fully and without tolls as the fragile US-Iran ceasefire teeters on the brink of collapse.

item.title: Fungus from NASA cleanrooms survived simulated Mars trip
item.description:
A fungus found lurking in NASA's ultra-clean spacecraft assembly rooms could withstand the punishing conditions of a trip to Mars and persist on the planet's surface, according to new research that raises fresh questions about keeping other worlds free from Earth's biology.

The study, published this week in Applied and Environmental Microbiology, is the first to demonstrate that a microbial eukaryote — a complex, nucleus-bearing organism — could survive every phase of a Mars mission, from pre-launch preparation through space travel to robotic surface exploration.

item.title: Trump to consider lifting Hormuz blockade after Pakistan army chief's call
item.description:
U.S. President Donald Trump told Pakistan's Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir in a phone call that he would consider his advice on lifting the Strait of Hormuz naval blockade, a Pakistani security source said on Monday, in a development that could open a path to resuming stalled peace talks with Iran as a ceasefire nears expiration.

The exchange came as a U.S. delegation was set to travel to Islamabad on Monday for a second round of Pakistan-brokered negotiations, though Tehran has not confirmed whether it will attend.

item.title: White House says US ready to back UAE financially amid Iran war
item.description:
White House National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett confirmed on Monday that the United States is prepared to provide financial assistance to the United Arab Emirates should the ongoing war with Iran further damage the Gulf state's economic outlook, though he indicated Washington does not expect such a step will be necessary.

The remarks follow a report by The Wall Street Journal that UAE Central Bank Governor Khaled Mohamed Balama raised the prospect of establishing a currency-swap line with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and officials from the Federal Reserve during meetings in Washington last week. No formal request for a swap line has been submitted, and Emirati representatives framed the discussions as a "preliminary and precautionary measure".

item.title: Iran signals possible return to US talks after initial rejection
item.description: The prospect of a second round of US-Iran peace talks in Islamabad swung between collapse and cautious revival on Monday as Tehran initially rejected participation, only to signal later in the day that it was "positively reviewing" a return to the negotiating table, according to a senior Iranian official who spoke to Reuters. The diplomatic whiplash came just two days before a fragile ceasefire between the two sides is set to expire on Wednesday, April 22.

item.title: Trump says Iran ceasefire extension 'highly unlikely' as talks falter
item.description: President Donald Trump said Monday it is "highly unlikely" he will extend the two-week ceasefire with Iran if no agreement is reached before it expires on Wednesday, warning that military strikes on bridges and power plants could follow and that the naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz will remain in place until a deal is signed.
